title: SEC0: compute_chat_id used as own oracle in delivery tests
description: In both full_message_delivery (harness.rs:390) and offline_delivery_and_retry (harness.rs:640), the chat_id is produced by calling compute_chat_id (the production function) and then that same value is put into the Peer/deliver request body, which is validated on bob's side by calling compute_chat_id again. There is no independently-computed expected chat_id value (e.g. a hardcoded hex string computed offline or via a second algorithm). If compute_chat_id has a bug that produces a consistent wrong answer, both the sender and the receiver agree, and the tests pass without catching the bug. The test's 'oracle' for chat_id correctness is the code under test itself. Fix: hardcode the expected chat_id as a hex literal computed offline (e.g. via sha256sum in a shell script or Python) and assert that compute_chat_id returns that value before using it in the test.
